Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Heard Miss.Soubhagya Vakkund on behalf of Sri.Y.Lakshmikanth Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant - claimant and Smt.Anusha Sangami on behalf of Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent - Insurance Company.
3.
Claimant is in appeal challenging the validity of judgment and award passed in MVC No.1035/2014 on the file of Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari dated 27.09.2016.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Admitted facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3411 Claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 25.09.2013 at about 2.45 p.m. involving lorry bearing No.HR-55/P-3065 and thus laid a claim before the Tribunal for awarding suitable compensation.
5. Claim petition, on contest, came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.1,26,000/- as under:

Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
Medical expenses incurred, Rs.18,800/-
 attendant, conveyance,
 nourishing food and other  incidental expenses  Loss of income during laid Rs.15,000/-
 up period

Loss of future income on Rs.67,200/-
 account of permanent  disability  Loss of amenities, life Rs.15,000/-
 comforts and expecting of  life  Total Rs.1,26,000/-
6.
Being not satisfied with the adequacy of compensation, claimant is in appeal.

Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Miss.Soubhagya Vakkund on behalf of Sri.Y.Lakshmikanth Reddy, learned counsel for the claimant vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not taken disability factor and monthly income in a proper manner and sought for enhancement of compensation.

8. She further contended that award of Rs.10,000/- on the head of pain and suffering is on lower side especially when the claimant has suffered two fractures and sought for enhancement of compensation.

9. Per contra, Smt.Anusha Sangami on behalf of Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment by contending that as per the law prevailed at the time of passing award, awarding compensation in a sum of Rs.1,26,000/- is just and proper.
10. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

sentences.text: On such perusal of material on record, it is crystal clear that the claimant has been successful in establishing that he met with a road traffic accident and suffered injuries including two fractures.
12. Therefore, awarding compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- on the head of pain and suffering is on lower side.

13. Likewise, monthly income should have been considered in a sum of Rs.7,000/- and when the doctor has assessed disability at 26%, 1/3rd of the same should have been taken by the Tribunal which would work out to 9% approximately.
14. Therefore, there is scope for enhancement of compensation on the head of loss of future income due to disability.
15. Instead of enhancing the compensation on each and every head, if a sum of Rs.85,000/- is enhanced over and above Rs.1,26,000/-, ends of justice would be met.

In view of the foregoing discussion, following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal stands modified.
(iii) As against Rs.1,26,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is entitled to Rs.2,11,000/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
(iv) Insurance Company is granted four weeks time to deposit the compensation amount.
